solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Primarily, missing a bar can ruin a fantastic piece of music

indicators.note: fantastic means wild and fanciful, so the gathered letters are rearranged freely
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A careless performer who skips a bar could spoil a splendid composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primarily' takes M from 'missing'; 'fantastic' shuffles M, A, BAR, CAN, RUIN and A into the Orff work.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Orff's cantata of medieval songs is a famous choral work, an example of a piece of music.

clue.text: Upstanding member breaks rules for friend

indicators.note: breaks means bursts into the middle of another word

parts.note: a code is a set of rules

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A respectable member of some club flouts its regulations for the sake of a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'Upstanding' reads the limb bottom to top, and 'breaks' pushes that reversal into the middle of the rule book's word.
explanation.definitionFit: A comrade is a companion or fellow, a synonym for a friend.

clue.text: Eg returns anew, being this?

indicators.note: anew means made over again in a fresh form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that keeps coming back afresh could be described by the very word being hinted at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anew' rearranges the letters of EG RETURNS; and something that returns anew is, by its nature, rising again.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurgent means rising again or reviving, which is what anything that returns anew is doing.

clue.text: Horrified grimace right off indicates stress

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a rictus is a fixed, gaping grimace, often one of horror

explanation.surface: A face frozen in horror signals that someone is under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes R from RICTUS; 'indicates' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody an ictus is the metrical beat or emphasis falling on a syllable, a kind of stress.

clue.text: Apt to take off clothes after embracing one

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the outer word dresses, surrounds, the inner

parts.note: to take off someone is to mimic them, to ape

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, holding something within

parts.note: post means after, as in post-war
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is inclined to strip off after a cuddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off clothes' reads as undressing, but 'take off' is mimicry and 'clothes' a containment verb; 'embracing' puts the numeral inside 'after' first.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite means well suited or relevant to the occasion, a synonym for apt.

clue.text: More work, you said, needed on cracked patio

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is reduced to its sound

parts.note: the word you, spoken, is the letter U

indicators.note: cracked means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A builder is told that more labour is required on a damaged patio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is Sir Thomas More, not 'extra'. 'cracked' turns PATIO into TOPIA, placed under U in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's 1516 book describing an ideal island commonwealth is titled with this name, so it is his work.

clue.text: Overshadow a stupid judge

parts.note: dumb means stupid
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A foolish magistrate is outshone by colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate can mean to foreshadow or overshadow, casting a shade over something.

clue.text: Flower maiden abandoned by ruler

indicators.note: abandoned by means left behind by, so the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a master is one who rules over others
M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman is jilted by a king.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, written M on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: The aster is a daisy-like garden plant, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Thankyou letter half written, receiving new gift

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so one piece goes inside
only half of the word is set down, its first three letters

explanation.surface: A half-finished thank-you note is sent along with a fresh present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half written' keeps the first three of LETTER's six letters, and 'receiving' sets N inside that half.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural aptitude, often called a gift.

clue.text: Teacher having favourite on reflection is a bad move

parts.note: Miss is how British pupils address a female teacher

indicators.note: a reflection shows a thing back to front, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A teacher who thinks it over realises that having a favourite pupil is unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns PET into TEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A misstep is literally a wrong step, so figuratively a blunder or bad move.

clue.text: Prickly sort wrecked uncovered Fiat Punto

indicators.note: wrecked means smashed up, so the letters are thrown into a new order
uncovered means with its outer covering stripped, leaving only the inner letters

explanation.surface: A grumpy motorist smashed up a convertible Fiat Punto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' leaves IA from FIAT, and 'wrecked' rearranges IA with PUNTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Opuntia is the prickly pear cactus genus, so it is a spiny kind of plant.

clue.text: Hanging around in disarray

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the letters are read backwards
in means the letters sit inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A curtain or tapestry is left draped untidily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks SARRA out of disarray and 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a tapestry wall-hanging, named after the French town famous for weaving them.

clue.text: Scoundrel carries torch for poet

indicators.note: carries means holds within, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a swine is a contemptible person, a scoundrel
to torch something is to set fire to it, burn it

explanation.surface: A villain is still holding a flame for a versifier he admires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torch' looks like a noun carried by the scoundrel, but it is the verb meaning set alight, which 'carries' places inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon Charles Swinburne was a Victorian English writer of verse, so he is a poet.

clue.text: Earl consumed by depression and sloth?

definitions.note: the question mark shows sloth is one example of the group

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A nobleman is brought low by melancholy and idleness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloth' looks like the deadly sin of laziness, but here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentates are toothless mammals such as sloths, anteaters and armadillos, so a sloth is one.

clue.text: Spike eats passion fruit

indicators.note: eats means takes in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a tine is a prong or spike, as on a fork
anger is a strong passion, rage

explanation.surface: Someone called Spike devours a passion fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passion fruit' reads as one item but splits into 'passion' for the inner piece and 'fruit' for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small orange-like citrus, an example of a fruit.

clue.text: Bun or waffle?

definitions.meaning: bun is a pet name for a bunny
to waffle is to talk on at length

explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Bun' and 'waffle' look like bakery or breakfast items.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunny is a small long-eared animal, and Britons rabbiting on are chattering aimlessly, both senses of the one word.

clue.text: Squad dug up a concealed danger

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a party is a group or squad, as in a search party
a dug is an udder or teat, slang for a breast, a boob

explanation.surface: A team excavated something hidden and hazardous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dug' looks like a past tense but is the noun; 'up' reverses PARTY then BOOB together.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby trap is a hidden device set to explode or harm when disturbed, a concealed danger.

clue.text: Charlie is put in grave briefly — that's a mistake

indicators.note: put in means placed inside another word
briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: grave means serious, solemn
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie is laid in his tomb too soon, which is an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a burial place but is the adjective; 'briefly' drops its final N, and 'put in' places C and the clue's 'is' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a grammatical blunder or breach of etiquette, so a mistake.

clue.text: Caretaker's bill can start to grow

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a tin is a can

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A janitor's invoice may begin to mount up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caretaker's' means 'Caretaker is', with the apostrophe s as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A caretaker manager or government is a stand-in one, serving temporarily in the role.

clue.text: Daughter wraps a present? On the contrary, getting stick

indicators.note: wraps means encloses, one piece going round another
on the contrary turns the relation around, so the daughter is wrapped rather than doing the wrapping

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A daughter gift-wraps a present and gets told off for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wraps' with 'On the contrary' means D goes inside A HERE rather than around it. 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or stay fixed to a surface, as glue does, a synonym of the verb stick.

clue.text: Recognises vocal person who's patient having special operations

indicators.note: vocal means spoken, so the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: recognises means knows, the word said aloud
Job is the biblical figure proverbial for patience
's is a short form of has, as in Job's got it

explanation.surface: Someone identifies a talkative hospital patient who is having specialist surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks like a hospital patient, but here it is the adjective: Job, of the Bible, was patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoplasty, cosmetic reshaping of the nose, is colloquially called this; these are particular surgical procedures.

clue.text: One visibly too hot for this garment

definitions.meaning: someone who perspires, showing they are overheated
a woollen top, a pullover or jumper

explanation.walkthrough: 'for this' joins the two senses: someone who perspires, and the knitted top that makes them do it.
explanation.definitionFit: The knitted top is called that because it was first worn to make athletes perspire; and anyone perspiring is literally one.

clue.text: Crib from administrator heartlessly

indicators.note: without its heart, the central letter is removed

parts.note: a manager is one who administers

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted official is caught cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crib' looks like copying, but it is the Nativity cradle; 'heartlessly' takes the middle A from MANAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A manger is a feeding trough, and the infant Jesus's crib in the nativity story was one.

clue.text: Add dash to publicity about female artist on vacation

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: hype is exaggerated publicity
a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone wants to spice up the promotion of a woman painter who is away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties ARTIST to its two outer letters; 'about' wraps the publicity word round the female bird and those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To hyphenate is to join words with a short line, literally inserting a dash.

clue.text: Mark has a beer, getting round in

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a pint is a glass of beer
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A man named Mark drinks a beer and buys the next round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a round of drinks but is just the letter O; 'has' and 'getting' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A point is a dot or small mark, and also a mark scored in a game.

clue.text: Cooks use it to season bird, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means heard, so the word is replaced by its sound-alike

parts.note: bird is British slang for a prison sentence, time inside

explanation.surface: Cooks use something to flavour a chicken, so we hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' looks like the poultry to be seasoned, but it is rhyming-slang 'bird lime' for time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic herb is a common kitchen seasoning, so it is what cooks add for flavour.

clue.text: Old boater maybe capsizes on English lake

indicators.note: capsizes means turns upside down, so in a down clue the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a boater is a straw hat, one example of a hat

explanation.surface: An elderly rower tips his craft over on a lake in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boater' looks like a rower but is a straw hat; 'capsizes' reverses O HAT to TAHO above E.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Tahoe is a large freshwater lake on the California-Nevada border.

clue.text: Trouble penetrating sound barrier

indicators.note: penetrating means going inside

parts.note: a ring is a sound, as of a bell
to ail is to trouble, as in what ails you

explanation.surface: Problems in breaking through the sound barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound barrier' reads as one phrase but splits into 'sound' for RING and 'barrier' for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A railing is a fence of rails, a kind of barrier.

clue.text: Anyhow, heir in time has to do this?

definitions.text: Anyhow, heir in time has to do this?

indicators.note: anyhow means in a haphazard way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Whatever happens, someone due to succeed must eventually come into the estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anyhow' jumbles HEIR, IN and T; and the whole clue says what every heir must one day do.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to receive property on someone's death, which is the destiny of an heir.

clue.text: Death penalty's introduction is accepted by regime, rather oddly

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are rearranged
introduction means the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: The death penalty is brought back by a government, rather surprisingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduction' takes P from penalty's; 'oddly' shuffles P with REGIME and RATHER. 'is accepted by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooded skeleton with a scythe is the traditional personification of death.
